newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa gold shares slide again as bullion bleeds. [CORRECTED 15:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: S.Africa gold shares slide again as bullion bleeds. [CORRECTED 15:40 GMT]

text.p: South African gold shares fell on Thursday in the face of an ailing bullion price which dragged the Johannesburg Stock Exchange's all gold index to its lowest level in four years. (Corrects from "its lowest level ever".) Dealers said, however, that shares were holding up better than the market had expected considering the gold price's slide below $338 an ounce at one stage, and as further losses in the metal were predicted.
"We expected them to do a lot worse. With gold cumulatively coming down about $5 in the past 24 hours, we were expecting a bloodbath," a trader of gold equities said.
Bullion fixed $1.55 down at $341.45 on Wednesday morning, continuing weaker in the afternoon, and was seen nearing its February 12 low of $336.15, the lowest in almost four years.

At 1315 GMT, the JSE 100 percent gold index was off 24.8 points or nearly two percent at 1,245.6. The gold index last broke below this level in April 1993. (Corrects to show index has previously been lower.)
But dealers said the move down had been slow in mediocre volumes.
"There is no panic. We even saw some offshore and local buying this morning. But some locals have turned sellers this afternoon," a trader said.
Amongst shares bellwether Vaal Reefs lost 300 cents to 272 rand, Freegold fell 25 cents to 29.80 rand and Dries shaved 35 cents to 41 rand.
